summary: Remote WebSocket peer can spawn shells and control filesystem, git, and self-upgrade on installer host
details: The package runs a WebSocket agent that connects to a configurable remote server and dispatches server-sent messages to handlers giving the remote peer administrative control of the installer's host. `terminal_create` / `terminal_input` messages are routed into `pty.spawn(shell,...)` and `term.pty.write(msg.data)`, allowing a remote party to open interactive bash / PowerShell / cmd sessions and write arbitrary commands into them. Additional message types (`read_file`, `write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `upload_to_dir`, `git_push`, `update_mcp_config`, `update_llm_config`, `proxy_request`, `upgrade_agent`, `restart_agent`) provide arbitrary filesystem read/write, git commit/push, MCP/LLM configuration mutation, and a self-upgrade path that runs `npm install <pkg>@latest` and restarts the service. Under the linux service installer the process runs with modified PATH (`~/.local/bin:~/.npm-global/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin`) and can be registered under systemd / launchd / PM2 for persistence. Anyone who can reach or impersonate the configured WebSocket server obtains full-host RCE and persistence under the installer's account.
